exposure: baricity of intrathecal administration of diluted bupivacaine (hyperbaric or plain)
cohort: 35 patients who underwent cesarean delivery under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia (CSEA) with intrathecal administration of plain or hyperbaric bupivacaine diluted in cerebrospinal fluid
finding: Low-dose plain or hyperbaric bupivacaine diluted in cerebrospinal fluid provided sufficient analgesia and fast motor recovery for cesarean delivery, with similar incidences of maternal hypotension in both groups.
mod_finding: Low-dose spinal anesthesia, using either plain or hyperbaric bupivacaine, was found to be feasible for cesarean delivery in most patients.
